ingest_queue.shape: Pure factory createPendingRetryQueue() returns closure over Map<eventId, PendingEntry>. FIFO via Map insertion order. Bounded (200), TTL (24h). Already has 12 unit tests (enqueue/dedupe/FIFO/remove/snapshot/cap-eviction/TTL/fallback-clock/validation).
ingest_queue.ttl_quirk: Age computed from event.created_at when within ±1y of now; otherwise falls back to local queuedAt timestamp (handles clock-skewed events).
ingest_queue.s6_relationship: retryAttempts (S6) lives in device-sync, NOT in ingest-queue. The queue does not know about retry counts. S6 calls retryQueue.snapshot() then filters externally.

task_store.owns: UI-facing consumer of decrypted task data. Two effects: load (49-66) and applicationMessage listener (69-99). dispatch (101+) writes locally + persists + sends to MLS group.
task_store.f3d_race: Load effect calls loadEvents(groupId) async; on resolve setState(restored). Listener does setState(applyEvent(stateRef.current, taskEvent)) on live event. If live event arrives while load pending, late setState(restored) overwrites the live update — restored may not include live event because device-sync's persistence listener writes are async.
task_store.two_listeners: device-sync.ts:475-494 PERSISTS to IDB regardless of UI mount. task-store.tsx:72-98 updates REACT STATE. Comment at task-store.tsx:87 documents the split — must NOT be collapsed.

gaps_and_risks_for_implementer.summary: TaskEvent has no id field — only type and content. Spec assumes 'taskEventId = TaskEvent.id'.
gaps_and_risks_for_implementer.where: src/store/task-events.ts (TaskEvent definition); referenced in spec.md TraceEvent shape (publish-task, task-store-accepted) and AC-DIAG-3a.
options: (a) Add an id field to TaskEvent (changes serialization, affects task-reducer and persistence).
(b) Use a content hash as the correlator — sha256(JSON.stringify(taskEvent)) computed at dispatch and re-derivable at receive.
(c) Use the rumor.id as the canonical correlator throughout, drop taskEventId from trace shape.
gaps_and_risks_for_implementer.recommendation: Option (c) is cheapest — rumor.id is unique per send (rumor includes pubkey+createdAt+content) and is already known at every emit point. Replace 'taskEventId' field references in spec/ACs with rumorId. Architect to confirm before S2 implementation.

gaps_and_risks_for_implementer.summary: sendApplicationRumor does not return the kind-445 relay event id. The publish-task trace event needs to bridge rumorId → kind-445 eventId, but marmot-ts wraps the publish internally.
gaps_and_risks_for_implementer.where: task-store.tsx:dispatch (~138) calls group.sendApplicationRumor(rumor) — no return value carrying kind-445 id.
options: (a) Patch marmot-ts to return the kind-445 event id from sendApplicationRumor (out of epic scope per AC-X-NO-MARMOT-CHANGE-1).

(b) Sender's own subscription replay: when device-sync.ts sees a kind-445 in sub-event whose decryption yields a rumor we just sent, emit publish-task at THAT moment. Means publish-task lags by one round-trip but the bridge is reliable.
(c) Store rumorId in a sender-side WeakSet/Map at dispatch time; correlate inside ingestGroupEventsRaw when a matching rumor decrypts on the sender's own page.
(d) Compute the kind-445 event id deterministically from the wrapper inputs at dispatch time (requires inspecting marmot-ts internals).
gaps_and_risks_for_implementer.recommendation: Option (c) is cleanest. Track Map<rumorId, {taskEventId, dispatchedAt}> in device-sync.ts; when ingest yields a processed result whose rumor.id matches, emit publish-task with both ids. The architect should confirm this approach early in S2.

gaps_and_risks_for_implementer.summary: Spec and ACs reference CI extensively (AC-X-CI-1, AC-DOC-3, AC-DOC-4) but no CI infrastructure exists in this repo.
gaps_and_risks_for_implementer.where: playwright.config.ts retries gates on process.env.CI today; AC-X-CI-1 says '10 consecutive CI runs'; AC-DOC-4 says '50 consecutive CI runs'.
options: (a) Recast all 'CI runs' as 'local make e2e runs'. Acceptance becomes time-on-machine, not pipeline.
(b) Stand up minimal GitHub Actions CI (out of epic scope; would need its own spec).
(c) Document the gap and accept that AC-X-CI-1 / AC-DOC-4 are satisfied by local runs in the report.md.
gaps_and_risks_for_implementer.recommendation: Option (c) for this epic; architect updates AC language to 'local consecutive runs' and the report.md captures the actual run count. Filing a separate spec for CI is out of scope.

gaps_and_risks_for_implementer.summary: multi-user-diag.spec.ts is gated by DIAG=1 (env var skip), not test.fixme as the spec wrote.
gaps_and_risks_for_implementer.where: e2e/tests/multi-user-diag.spec.ts:35 — process.env.DIAG === '1' check inside test body.
options: (a) S3's harness builds on the existing DIAG=1 gate — adds NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_TRACE_MLS=1 as a second gate (so trace dumps only happen when both are set).
(b) Replace the DIAG gate with NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_TRACE_MLS as the only gate.
(c) Keep DIAG gate as 'should this test run at all' and use NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_TRACE_MLS as 'should it dump traces.'
gaps_and_risks_for_implementer.recommendation: Option (c) preserves existing behavior — the diagnostic test is opt-in (DIAG=1) and additionally can dump traces if NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_TRACE_MLS=1. AC-DIAG-1 wording 'no longer fixme-marked' should be reworded to 'kept under DIAG=1 gate; runs with full trace capture when both DIAG=1 and NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_TRACE_MLS=1'.
